what_its_for: Crizanlizumab is used to help reduce the number of painful crises (called vaso-occlusive crises or VOCs) in adults and children 16 years and older who have sickle cell disease. Sickle cell disease causes abnormal red blood cells that can block blood flow and cause severe pain episodes. This medicine works by blocking a protein that causes blood cells to stick together and clog blood vessels.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it is slowly injected into a vein through an IV line by a healthcare provider in a clinic or infusion center. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes. Your doctor will set up a schedule for your infusion appointments.
dosing: The usual dose is 5 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given through an IV. You will receive it at Week 0 (your first dose), then again at Week 2, then once every 4 weeks after that. Your healthcare team will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. Always attend your scheduled infusion appointments to get the most benefit from this medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss or cannot attend a scheduled infusion appointment, contact your healthcare provider right away to reschedule as soon as possible. After a missed dose, your next dose will be given 2 weeks later, and then you will return to the regular every-4-week schedule. Do not skip doses if you can avoid it, as regular dosing is important to help prevent pain crises.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home since it is prepared and given by healthcare professionals at an infusion center or clinic. The prepared infusion should be used within 4.5 hours if kept at room temperature, or within 24 hours if kept in the refrigerator. Protect the medicine from light and do not freeze it.
what_to_avoid: Talk to your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some may interact with crizanlizumab. Let your healthcare team know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before receiving this medicine. Avoid activities that could increase your risk of injury during treatment, and report any unusual pain or symptoms to your doctor right away.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency care right away if you experience: sudden or severe pain during or after your infusion, nausea, vomiting, tiredness, fever, or chills during your infusion (signs of an infusion reaction), signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness, unusual or new pain that is different from your normal sickle cell pain, or any other unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Crizanlizumab does not work right away like a pain reliever. It works over time to help lower how often you have pain crises. Some patients may start to see fewer pain episodes after a few months of regular treatment. It is important to keep attending your infusion appointments even if you feel well, because the medicine works best when taken consistently.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or Liver Problems: No dose adjustment is currently recommended for patients with kidney or liver problems, but let your doctor know about any existing conditions. Children: This medicine is only approved for patients 16 years of age and older. Safety and effectiveness in younger children have not been established.
